name: attribute-invalid-any-units-not-empty
description: The pseudo unit class anyUnits lists a unit or has defaultUnits.
common_causes: Adding units under anyUnits as if it were an ordinary unit class
Giving anyUnits a defaultUnits attribute
explanation: anyUnits (specification 4.0.0, section 3.1.4.4) is a pseudo unit class: a placeholder with unitClass=anyUnits accepts a value with or without a unit, and any unit of any unit class of the schema. The class itself must list no units and must have no defaultUnits: a value without a unit on such a placeholder is valid but has no default unit and no conversion.
correction_strategy: Keep anyUnits empty; put real units in their own unit classes

correction_examples.explanation: anyUnits lists no units
anyUnits has no default

correction_patterns: anyUnits is empty
No defaultUnits on anyUnits
fix_instructions: 1. Remove any unit lines under anyUnits
2. Remove any defaultUnits attribute from anyUnits
validation_hints: Applies to any schema that defines a unit class named anyUnits

correction_strategy: Add valueClass=numericClass to the placeholder, or remove the unit class if the value is not a number

name: attribute-duplicate-node-derived-in-two-classes
description: A unit string is derived by two unit classes (SI modifier applied to a unit of each) and listed by neither, so it would be ambiguous on a placeholder that accepts any unit.
common_causes: Two SI unit symbols in different classes whose modified forms coincide (da + Q and d + aQ both give daQ)
explanation: Specification 4.0.0 lets a placeholder accept a unit from any unit class (unitClass=anyUnits), so every unit string must resolve to one class. A string listed in one class and derived in another is fine: the listed unit wins. A string that two classes derive and neither lists has no winner and is a SCHEMA_DUPLICATE_NODE error. Two classes listing the same unit is already a duplicate node.
correction_strategy: Rename or drop one of the units so that no modified form coincides, or list the shared form in one class

correction_examples.wrong: qUnits lists Q and aqUnits lists aQ with modifiers d and da: daQ is da+Q and d+aQ
correction_examples.correct: Remove the da modifier, or list daQ in one class
correction_examples.explanation: A string may be derived by at most one class unless some class lists it

correction_patterns: One class per derivable string
Listed wins over derived
fix_instructions: 1. Expand every SI unit of every class with every applicable modifier
2. Find strings produced by two classes that no class lists
3. Change one of the units or modifiers involved
validation_hints: Build the set of derived forms per class; a form in two classes and not listed anywhere is the error
A form listed in one class and derived in another is allowed

name: library-invalid-duplicate-value-class
description: An unmerged partnered library schema declares a value class whose name already exists in its standard schema partner.
common_causes: Copying a value class from the standard schema into the library instead of relying on the partner
Reusing a standard value class name for a library-specific value format
explanation: An unmerged partnered library schema may not declare a schema element (tag, unit, unit class, unit modifier, value class, or schema attribute) with the same name as an element of its standard schema partner. The value class nameClass already exists in the standard schema, so declaring it in the library is a duplication. The standard schema's value classes are available to the library automatically through the partnering.
correction_strategy: Remove the duplicated value class from the library, or give the library's value class a new name if it is genuinely different.

correction_examples.explanation: nameClass duplicates a standard schema value class; a new name that does not exist in the partner is merged directly.

specification_reference: Appendix B. SCHEMA_LIBRARY_INVALID (i); 7.4.3. Partnered design rules

name: library-invalid-duplicate-schema-attribute
description: An unmerged partnered library schema declares a schema attribute whose name already exists in its standard schema partner.
common_causes: Copying a schema attribute from the standard schema into the library instead of relying on the partner
Reusing a standard schema attribute name for a library-specific attribute
explanation: An unmerged partnered library schema may not declare a schema element (tag, unit, unit class, unit modifier, value class, or schema attribute) with the same name as an element of its standard schema partner. The schema attribute suggestedTag already exists in the standard schema, so declaring it in the library is a duplication. The standard schema's attributes are available to the library automatically through the partnering.
correction_strategy: Remove the duplicated schema attribute from the library, or give the library's attribute a new name if it is genuinely different.

correction_examples.explanation: suggestedTag duplicates a standard schema attribute; a new attribute name that does not exist in the partner is merged directly.

specification_reference: Appendix B. SCHEMA_LIBRARY_INVALID (i); 7.4.3. Partnered design rules

name: library-invalid-duplicate-unit-modifier
description: An unmerged partnered library schema declares a unit modifier whose name already exists in its standard schema partner.
common_causes: Copying a unit modifier from the standard schema into the library instead of relying on the partner
Reusing a standard unit modifier name for a library-specific scale factor
explanation: An unmerged partnered library schema may not declare a schema element (tag, unit, unit class, unit modifier, value class, or schema attribute) with the same name as an element of its standard schema partner. The unit modifier deca already exists in the standard schema, so declaring it in the library is a duplication. The standard schema's unit modifiers are available to the library automatically through the partnering.
correction_strategy: Remove the duplicated unit modifier from the library, or give the library's unit modifier a new name if it is genuinely different.

correction_examples.explanation: deca duplicates a standard schema unit modifier; a new modifier name that does not exist in the partner is merged directly.

specification_reference: Appendix B. SCHEMA_LIBRARY_INVALID (i); 7.4.3. Partnered design rules

name: library-invalid-rooted-in-unpartnered
description: The rooted attribute appears in an unpartnered library schema, whose header has no withStandard attribute.
common_causes: Using the rooted attribute in a library that is not partnered with a standard schema
Forgetting the withStandard header attribute when designing a partnered library
explanation: The rooted attribute anchors a library node under a node of the standard schema partner, so it is only meaningful in a schema whose header has both the library and withStandard attributes. This library schema has the library attribute but no withStandard attribute (it is unpartnered), so there is no partner to root into and the rooted attribute is invalid.
correction_strategy: Either partner the library by adding withStandard to the header, or remove the rooted attribute from the node.

correction_examples.correct: HED version="1.0.0" library="testconflict" withStandard="8.4.0" unmerged="True" with '''NewTag''' {rooted=Event}
correction_examples.explanation: With a withStandard partner in the header the rooted attribute has a standard schema to anchor into.

name: library-invalid-unpartnered-properties-allowed
description: An unpartnered library schema may declare its own schema attributes and a non-empty Properties section.
common_causes: Applying the empty-Properties rule for unmerged partnered libraries to unpartnered libraries as well
explanation: The rule that a Properties section must be empty applies only to unmerged partnered library schemas, which get their properties from the standard schema partner. An unpartnered library schema is self-contained: it must declare the schema attributes its tags use and the properties that describe those attributes, so a non-empty Properties section is valid and required here.
correction_strategy: No correction needed; validators must accept schema attributes and properties declared in an unpartnered library schema.

correction_examples.wrong: Rejecting a Properties section in an unpartnered library schema
correction_examples.correct: Reject a non-empty Properties section only in an unmerged partnered library schema
correction_examples.explanation: Only partnered libraries inherit properties from a standard schema partner; unpartnered libraries must define their own.

specification_reference: Appendix B. SCHEMA_LIBRARY_INVALID (j); 7.4.2. Unpartnered design rules

name: library-invalid-properties-in-unmerged
description: An unmerged partnered library schema has a non-empty Properties section.
common_causes: Copying the standard schema's Properties section into an unmerged partnered library
Confusing the unmerged partnered form with the self-contained unpartnered form, which must declare its own properties
explanation: An unmerged partnered library schema never defines schema properties: its Properties section must be empty, because the properties come from the standard schema partner when the schema is loaded. Declaring any property in the unmerged form - even one copied verbatim from the partner - is invalid. (An unpartnered library, by contrast, must declare its own properties; see library-invalid-unpartnered-properties-allowed.)
correction_strategy: Empty the Properties section of the unmerged partnered library; the standard schema partner supplies the properties.

correction_examples.explanation: The unmerged partnered form leaves the section empty; the properties come from the standard schema partner.

specification_reference: Appendix B. SCHEMA_LIBRARY_INVALID (j); 7.4.3. Partnered design rules

name: library-invalid-merged-rooted-not-under-anchor
description: In a merged library schema, a node with rooted=XXX must be a direct child of XXX.
common_causes: Editing a merged schema by hand and moving a rooted subtree to the top level
Saving a schema with a merged header (no unmerged attribute) without applying the rooted anchoring
explanation: The rooted attribute records where a library subtree is anchored in the standard schema. In unmerged form the rooted node must be at the top level; in merged form the anchoring has been applied, so a node with rooted=Event must appear as a direct child of Event. Here Rooted-tag carries rooted=Event but sits at the top level of a merged schema, so its placement contradicts the attribute. The passing schema places the same node directly under Event. (A merged schema carries its partner's Properties section verbatim and must define every attribute its elements use, so these fixtures include the 8.4.0 properties and the rooted and inLibrary attribute definitions.)
correction_strategy: Place the rooted node directly under its anchor node in the merged form, or save the schema in unmerged form (unmerged="True") with the rooted node at the top level.

correction_examples.wrong: Top-level '''Rooted-tag''' {rooted=Event, inLibrary=testconflict} in a merged schema
correction_examples.explanation: In merged form the rooted node has already been moved under its anchor, so it must appear as a direct child of Event.

name: library-invalid-merged-properties-mismatch
description: A merged partnered library schema's Properties section must be identical to that of its standard schema partner.
common_causes: Editing a property description by hand in the merged file
Merging against a different standard schema version than the withStandard partner
explanation: Library schemas never define schema properties, so the Properties section of a merged partnered library schema is exactly the Properties section of its standard schema partner. Here the description of the boolRange property differs from the 8.4.0 partner's text (the sentence about its former name is missing), so the Properties section differs from the partner and the schema is invalid. The passing schema carries the partner's Properties verbatim.
correction_strategy: Regenerate the merged form from the unmerged source with schema tools instead of editing it by hand; the Properties section must be the partner's, unchanged.

correction_examples.wrong: * boolRange <nowiki>[This schema attribute's value can be true or false.]</nowiki>
correction_examples.correct: * boolRange <nowiki>[This schema attribute's value can be true or false. This property was formerly named boolProperty.]</nowiki>
correction_examples.explanation: The merged form must reproduce the partner's property descriptions exactly.

specification_reference: Appendix B. SCHEMA_LIBRARY_INVALID (k); 7.3.3. Merged vs unmerged

name: library-invalid-reserved-in-unmerged
description: The reserved attribute cannot be used in an unmerged partnered library schema.
common_causes: Marking a partnered library node reserved instead of proposing the reserved tag for the standard schema
Copying a reserved node from the standard schema into a library
explanation: The reserved attribute marks nodes with special meaning or function and can appear only in standard schemas or unpartnered library schemas. An unmerged partnered library schema may not use it. The passing companion is an unpartnered library, which is self-contained and may declare the reserved schema attribute and use it on its own nodes.
correction_strategy: Remove the reserved attribute from the partnered library node; reserved tags belong to the standard schema or to a self-contained unpartnered library.

correction_examples.explanation: A partnered library node cannot be reserved; drop the attribute or move the tag to the standard schema.

name: schema-missing-extra
description: An extras section (Sources, Prefixes, or External annotations) has a row with an empty column value.
common_causes: A required column of an extras row was left empty when the row was added
A row was copied from a template and not all columns were filled in
The value was accidentally deleted while editing, leaving 'key=' with nothing after it
A placeholder row was committed before its real values were known
explanation: The extras sections of a HED schema (Sources, Prefixes, and External annotations) are tables in which every row must give a non-empty value in every column: source, link, and description in Sources; prefix, namespace, and description in Prefixes; prefix, id, iri, and description in External annotations. A row that supplies a column key but leaves its value empty (for example 'source=' or 'namespace=') is incomplete, and schema loading reports this warning. The sections themselves are optional in the file: a schema without them is loaded with empty extras sections, and their absence is not an error.
correction_strategy: Fill in every empty column of the flagged extras row, or delete the row entirely if there is no value to record

correction_examples.explanation: The 'source' column of a Sources row was empty; the source name was filled in
The 'namespace' column of a Prefixes row was empty; the ontology namespace was filled in
The 'id' column of an External annotations row was empty; the annotation id was filled in
The 'link' column of a Sources row was empty; every column of an extras row must have a value, not only the key column

specification_reference: 3.1.4.10. Optional extra sections; Appendix B SCHEMA_MISSING_EXTRA

name: schema-section-missing
description: A required schema section is missing from the schema file.
common_causes: Missing required schema sections
Sections not in correct order
Incorrect section markers or delimiters
Incomplete schema template usage
Copy-paste errors in schema creation
explanation: HED schemas must contain all required sections in the correct order: Prologue, Schema, Unit classes, Unit modifiers, Value classes, Schema attributes, Properties, and Epilogue. Missing or misplaced sections prevent proper schema validation.
correction_strategy: Add missing sections in correct order with proper delimiters

correction_examples.explanation: Added required section with proper MediaWiki formatting

correction_examples.correct: Reorder to: Prologue, Schema, Unit classes, Unit modifiers, Value classes, Schema attributes, Properties, Epilogue
correction_examples.explanation: Arranged sections in required sequence

correction_patterns: Include all required sections even if empty
Use proper section delimiters (''' for MediaWiki)
Follow exact section ordering requirements
Check section names match required format
Ensure proper start/end schema markers
fix_instructions: 1. Check for all required sections
2. Verify sections are in correct order
3. Add missing sections with proper delimiters
4. Ensure section names match requirements exactly
5. Validate schema structure completeness
validation_hints: Empty sections are allowed but must be present
Section order is strictly enforced
Use exact section names and formatting
Check both start and end markers
